thread.title: iPhone shipments have slowed in India — and it might signal a preference for lower-priced devices (AAPL)

title: iPhone shipments have slowed in India — and it might signal a preference for lower-priced devices (AAPL)
text:
iPhone shipments have slowed in India — and it might signal a preference for lower-priced devices (AAPL) Posted By: BusinessInsider July 18, 2018 This story was delivered to Business Insider Intelligence Apps and Platforms Briefing subscribers hours before appearing on Business Insider. To be the first to know, please click here .
iPhone sales in India were weak in the first half of 2018, with only 1 million estimated handset shipments in the region, according to Counterpoint Research, per Bloomberg. Apple sold 3.2 million handsets in India in 2017, but given the company’s slowing sales growth in the region, shipments are expected reach 2.4 million units in 2018.
As Apple looks to emerging markets for continued device and revenue growth, the slowdown in India could signal trouble for the company — iPhones accounted for nearly 70% of its fiscal Q2 2018 global revenue. India is the second-largest smartphone market in the world, and the fastest-growing smartphone market globally — the region saw smartphone shipments increase 14% year-over-year (YoY) in 2017.
iPhone sales in India are likely slowing because of their high price points. While the average selling price of smartphones in India is Rs10,733 ($157), iPhones cost between Rs35,000 ($500) and Rs80,000 ($1,100), according to Quartz.
This greatly inhibits the potential buyer pool for Apple’s flagship handsets. For instance, the best-selling smartphone in India in 2017 was the Xiaomi Redmi Note 4, which costs roughly Rs11,964 ($175). The high cost of iPhones is likely why Apple lags behind rivals in India’s smartphone market, accounting for less than 2% of smartphone shipments in India as of Q1 2018, behind Xiaomi (31%) and Samsung (26%).
Nevertheless, Apple’s lagging shipments could be short-lived given the company’s recent focus on the lower end of the smartphone market.Apple is reportedly planning to release lower-priced iPhones in the second half of 2018.
While this is a pivot from Apple’s strategy of catering to the high end of the market, consumers in developing markets typically prefer smartphones at low price points, and catering to this segment could drive uptake of its devices globally. Moreover, expanding its consumer base also exposes more users to Apple’s Services, such as the App Store.
Apple’s Services business is a growing revenue driver for the company and provides a continuous stream of revenue, compared to cyclical device purchasing behavior. In just the first half of 2018 alone, Apple raked in $22.6 billion in App Store revenue.
